feedback.problem:
If $f(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=-9$ and $f(-9)=4,$ then what is 
${lim}_{x\to (-9)^{-}}(f(x)-x)^{2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=-9,$ we must have

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-9)^{-}}f(x)=f(-9)=4.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-9)^{-}}(f(x)-x)^{2}=(4-(-9))^{2}=169.\end{aligned}
$$
